issues.title: Schrödinger trajectory-space claim exceeds the paper's formal support

failure_location.quote: the data space spanned by the average of the solution trajectory can be approximated by the linear space of logarithmic dimension (see subsection \ref{schrodinger}),  whereas the data space spanned by the solution itself only admits polynomial-dimensional approximation.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For each $t$, $w_{\epsilon}$ is in the space

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that one logarithmic-dimensional linear space approximates the data space spanned by the entire mean Schrödinger trajectory, while the full stochastic trajectory only admits polynomial-dimensional approximation. The old paper actually states at most that, for each fixed t, there exists a space V, and the proof names it V_t; this does not supply one space controlling the trajectory over time. Unlike the hyperbolic result's L2([0,T];H) estimate, the Schrödinger section also gives no formal polynomial-dimensional guarantee or lower limitation for the full trajectory. The common-trajectory scope and the mean-versus-full comparison are therefore materially unsupported.
issues.overall_effect: A prominently advertised quantitative Schrödinger data-space contribution and its claimed contrast between mean and full trajectories are not established by the old analysis.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retract the advertised Schrödinger trajectory-space comparison wherever it appears. State only that the analysis supplies a possibly time-dependent approximating space for each fixed time, and make no claim that one logarithmic-dimensional space controls the mean trajectory or that the full trajectory has an "only polynomial" dimensional limitation. Retaining the original comparison would require new trajectory-level approximation and limitation theorems.
issues.why_classification: The fixed-time statement with spaces V_t is not recognizably comparable to a common-space guarantee for an entire trajectory, and no formal result supports the asserted mean-versus-full limitation. The available local rewrite therefore removes the central trajectory-space claim and its comparison, which is major mathematical loss; preserving them would require essentially new analysis.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: We present interesting findings on the data spaces associated with two types of linear SPDEs: parabolic and hyperbolic equations.

issues.title: Multiplicative Fourier formula is undefined on zero modes
issues.failure_explanation: For a multiplicative Fourier mode, an initially zero mode remains zero. The old ratio is then 0/0 and is undefined because no nonvanishing condition accompanies the displayed general solution formula. Later identification arguments explicitly restrict to nonzero modes, but that does not repair the standalone formula. Multiplying by the initial mode gives the valid identity on every mode.
issues.overall_effect: The general multiplicative Fourier solution display is not well-defined on admissible zero modes; the later nonzero-mode identification arguments themselves remain usable.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the quotient formula by the equivalent product identity for the Fourier mode, valid for every mode, and state the quotient version only when the initial mode is nonzero. Explicitly note that an initially zero multiplicative mode remains zero.
issues.why_classification: This is a genuine domain defect rather than a transcription error, but the invariant zero case and the product-form correction are immediate and local. They preserve the exact solution formula and leave all later arguments already restricted to nonzero modes unchanged.

issues.title: Schrödinger proposition uses a random subspace to approximate the mean
issues.failure_explanation: The assumptions allow each c_k to be an F_0-measurable random variable. Consequently, the generators containing c_k define an omega-dependent space rather than a fixed linear subspace of H_C. More directly, E[u_M] contains E[c_k], while the proposed w_epsilon contains c_k itself; the displayed Taylor-tail estimate silently drops this difference and later even replaces E[u_M] by u_M. Thus the projection argument does not prove the proposition for the allowed random initial data.
issues.overall_effect: The pointwise logarithmic-dimensional approximation proposition lacks a valid proof for its stated random-initial-data regime.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Let the deterministic mean coefficients be bar c_k = E[c_k]. Define the Taylor approximant and every generator of V_t using bar c_k rather than c_k, replace occurrences of u_M in the relevant estimates by E[u_M], and apply the large-time operator approximation to E[u_0]. The bound |E[c_k]|^2 <= E[|c_k|^2] then gives the same dimension and error estimate, while V_t is a fixed subspace and E[P_Vu] = P_VE[u].
issues.why_classification: The proof makes an invalid random-versus-mean inference, so the defect is not a typo. Nevertheless, linearity of expectation and Jensen's inequality repair the existing construction locally without a new lemma, an added assumption, or any loss of the random-initial-data regime, dimension, or approximation rate.

issues.title: Euler–Maruyama expansion overstates the multiplicative-noise remainder order
issues.failure_explanation: Take the paper's admissible multiplicative special case du=u dW and write h=Delta t. Its exact increment is u_t(exp(Delta W-h/2)-1). After subtracting the frozen Euler–Maruyama term u_t Delta W, the leading remainder is (u_t/2)((Delta W)^2-h), whose L2 norm is proportional to h, not h^(3/2). Thus the old displayed expansion is not a valid strong or pathwise estimate for the stated general multiplicative-noise model.
issues.overall_effect: The local stochastic expansion and its stated strong remainder order are invalid; the mean and covariance feature relations require separate weak or mean-square derivations rather than direct inheritance from that display.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the error mode and regularity assumptions explicitly and replace the frozen Euler–Maruyama expansion by one with an L2 remainder of order Delta t. Derive the mean increment and squared-residual covariance relations separately from the exact integral equation, deterministic quadrature estimates, conditional moments, and Ito isometry; under standard smoothness these can retain the appropriate weak and mean-square remainder orders.
issues.why_classification: The displayed order is a substantive false strong rate, not a notational slip. Merely changing it to order Delta t weakens the recorded expansion, while the downstream mean and covariance relations require a contained but nontrivial replacement argument rather than inheritance from that expansion. This does not require global reconstruction and preserves the identification method's leading relations, so the issue is moderate rather than serious.

issues.title: Terminal drift-response entry is identically zero
issues.failure_explanation: Every response row is meant to represent E[u(t_i,x_m)]-E[u(t_{i-1},x_m)]. The printed final row is E[u(t_I,x_M)]-E[u(t_I,x_M)]=0, so it does not correspond to the final time interval and is inconsistent with the associated regression construction.
issues.overall_effect: The printed drift regression uses an erroneous zero response in its final row, which can bias the fitted drift coefficients and any downstream residual computed from them.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the last response entry by E[u(t_I,x_M)] - E[u(t_{I-1},x_M)].
issues.why_classification: The preceding rows, the stated interval-increment definition, and the associated feature matrix uniquely force this index correction. No mathematical inference or construction must be changed.

issues.title: QSP expansion uses an undefined support index
issues.failure_explanation: The algorithm has iteration state ell and a current support I^ell; no state I^n is introduced. Therefore Step 1 does not specify which existing support must be retained during expansion, so the subsequent restricted minimization is not executable as printed.
issues.overall_effect: The old QSP pseudocode leaves its expanded support undefined and therefore does not determine the candidate variables for the next minimization.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the undefined support I^n in QSP Step 1 by the current support I^ell.
issues.why_classification: The algorithm has only the iteration index ell, and both the expansion description and subsequent steps uniquely require retaining I^ell. This is a transcriptional index error with a uniquely forced correction.

issues.title: Diffusion SAA argmin convergence fails on the exact-sparsity domain

failure_location.quote: Then the problem~\eqref{eq_L0_diffuse_select_sample} converges to~\eqref{eq_L0_diffuse_select} almost surely in the following sense.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem claims almost-sure optimal-value convergence and outer convergence of diffusion argmin sets while the drift parameter varies along a random convergent subsequence. Its assumptions provide only a local minimizer for each fixed drift parameter; they do not ensure a closed or compact feasible set, nonempty and level-bounded global argmin sets, or joint uniform convergence in the drift parameter. A direct admissible counterexample is obtained by taking every diffusion matrix and response to be zero. Then every exact-j vector is a local and global minimizer, so Pi_N=Pi_O={c: ||c||_0=j}; for j=1, vectors (1/N,0,...) belong to every Pi_N but converge to zero, which is not in Pi_O. Thus the claimed outer inclusion fails even for identical sample and population objectives. In addition, Phi_O(hat a) is defined using the free variable a rather than hat a.
issues.overall_effect: The old paper does not establish its advertised diffusion sample-average consistency guarantee for global optimal values or minimizer sets along estimated drift coefficients.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the theorem on a closed compact exact-sparsity set, for example a finite union over supports of size j with a common coefficient bound and a positive lower bound on active coefficients. Establish almost-sure uniform convergence of g_N(c,a_N) to g_O(c,a) on that set whenever a_N converges to a, correct Phi_O(hat a) to use hat a, and apply a standard uniform argmin-consistency theorem to obtain value and outer minimizer convergence.
issues.why_classification: The nonclosed exact-sparsity domain, absence of level-bounded global argmins, and lack of joint uniform convergence cannot be repaired by the stated local-minimizer assumption or a symbol edit. A compact separated-domain formulation and a replacement argmin argument are nontrivial, but they are contained within this theorem and preserve a recognizably comparable sample-average consistency guarantee under limited additional conditions.

issues.title: Stouffer additive-noise decision threshold is invalid

failure_location.quote: Then for some significance level $p^* \in (0,1)$, we decide that the diffusion part contains multiplicative noise if $2|Z_N|\geq \Phi^{-1}(p^*)$, and it is only additive if $2|Z_N|<\Phi^{-1}(p^*)/2$.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims a binary additive-versus-multiplicative decision. If p*<1/2, then Phi^{-1}(p*)<0, while 2|Z_N| is nonnegative, so the multiplicative inequality always holds and the additive inequality can never hold. At p*=1/2 the same degeneracy occurs. If p*>1/2, the thresholds Phi^{-1}(p*) and Phi^{-1}(p*)/2 leave a gap of values satisfying neither branch. Thus the old rule does not implement a valid significance test in any part of its stated range.
issues.overall_effect: For conventional small significance levels the procedure always routes data to general diffusion identification and can never select its advertised pure-additive branch; for larger levels it is not a complete decision rule.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the two-sided combined p-value as p_comb = 2(1 - Phi(|Z_N|)) and classify the noise as multiplicative when p_comb <= p*, and as additive otherwise. Equivalently, reject the additive null when |Z_N| >= Phi^{-1}(1-p*/2).
issues.why_classification: The original thresholds do not define a valid exhaustive significance rule, and their correction is not uniquely transcriptional. However, standard Stouffer calibration supplies a one-line local repair that preserves the same Gaussianity test, binary branches, and subsequent identification procedure without mathematical loss.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: If the combined $p$-value is smaller than some threshold $p^*>0$, we deem the noise to be multiplicative and proceed with the diffusion identification in Section~\ref{sec:QSP}. Otherwise, we treat it as additive

issues.title: Subspace Pursuit returns an undefined coefficient vector
issues.failure_explanation: Initialization defines only the support and residual. Step 2 defines an expanded-support vector bar c, and Step 3 again defines only a residual. No step defines hat c^(0) or hat c^(ell+1), yet Step 4 assigns hat c^(ell) to the advertised output. Hence the output coefficient vector is undefined, including when the first iteration triggers stopping.
issues.overall_effect: The printed SP procedure may identify a support but cannot execute its advertised coefficient-output contract.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: At initialization and after every support update, define a full coefficient vector by placing the restricted least-squares solution on the current support and zeros elsewhere. Undo the column normalization, or refit on the original feature matrix, before returning the final vector; use these defined iterates in the stopping branch.
issues.why_classification: The coefficient-output state is genuinely absent, so this is more than a single forced typographical substitution. The residual formulas already determine the requisite restricted least-squares fits, making the repair short and routine bookkeeping that leaves the support-search mechanism and output guarantee otherwise unchanged.
